Ipieca and IOGP (2022-2025). Energy efficiency compendium: technology and good-practice info sheets for the oil and gas industry. Ipieca, London (with the International Association of Oil & Gas Producers). https://www.ipieca.org/resources/energy-efficiency-compendium (25 PDF sheets downloaded 2026-10-06). Sheets (topic last reviewed): Alternative thermodynamic cycles (Nov 2022); Artificial lift (Jun 2023); Battery energy storage system (BESS) integration into power generation systems (May 2025); Combined-cycle gas turbines (Nov 2022); Combined heat and power (Nov 2022); Compressors (Nov 2022); Cooling systems (Nov 2022); Drilling rigs (Jun 2023); Ejectors (Nov 2022); Electric motors (Jun 2023); Energy-efficient design for carbon dioxide reduction (Nov 2022); Energy performance monitoring and optimization (Nov 2022); Flowlines and pipelines (Jun 2023); Fractionation columns (previously vacuum systems) (May 2025); Fuel-fired furnaces and boilers (Nov 2022); Gas turboexpanders (Jun 2023); Heat exchangers (Nov 2022); Heat pumps (Jun 2023); Liquid power recovery turbines (Jun 2023); Open-cycle gas turbines (Nov 2022); Passing valves (leakage) (Feb 2025); Pinch analysis (Nov 2022); Pumps (Nov 2022); Reducing venting in oil and gas operations (Feb 2025); Reducing flaring in oil and gas operations (Feb 2025). No DOI or report number printed.

ONE extraction for 25 sheets; process names the sheet and section; reference = sheet + printed page (each sheet is paginated from 1, printed page = PDF page of that sheet file, files kept as ipieca_2025_<sheet-slug>.pdf). Sheets dated Nov 2022 to May 2025 (id year 2025 = latest sheet); price year taken as each sheet year where unstated. SHEETS WITH USABLE NUMBERS (main file): Open-cycle gas turbines (33-43% aeroderivative at full load, up to 330 MW, 21 MW unit ~30% and 500 kg CO2/MWh); Alternative thermodynamic cycles (ORC 10-20%; upstream OCGT fleet 25-40%); Combined-cycle gas turbines (onshore 50-63%, ~60%; offshore <50%, ~50%; sizes); Combined heat and power (total CHP 60-80%; offshore 30 MWe GT + 35 MW WHRU; case studies: WHRU retrofit USD 5.0 M installed for 15.7 MWth, GT part-load and compressor-driver efficiencies derived from printed power/fuel, heater efficiencies 80%/88%, 15 MW polymer-plant CHP EUR 16 M, 77.3%/84.6%); Compressors (70->90% machine efficiency); Gas turboexpanders (up to 90%, 50 kW-15 MW, city gate 1.8 MW/6000 MWh/85%); Liquid power recovery turbines (40-80%, up to 1 MW, refinery 349 kW/2966 MWh); Pumps (VFD 53-97%); Fuel-fired furnaces and boilers (gas boilers 85-95% LHV, furnaces with APH 80-92% LHV, two refinery retrofit case studies with efficiencies, fired duty, stack temperatures); Heat pumps (building COP 2-5); BESS (Li-ion RTE 85-95/85-90%, 12 yr, TRL 11; flow 70-90%, 20 yr, TRL 9; rig retrofit -20-25% CO2); Drilling rigs (gas engines -20-25% CO2; grid up to -100%); Artificial lift (Table 1 overall system efficiency for 7 lift methods). MEASURES/OTHER-VALUES ONLY: Electric motors, Fractionation columns (steam vs liquid-jet ejector case, tray efficiencies), Pinch analysis, Energy performance monitoring, Energy-efficient design, Flowlines and pipelines, Ejectors, Heat exchangers, Cooling systems. NO NUMBERS: Passing valves, Reducing venting, Reducing flaring (pointers to IOGP Reports 467, 647, 673, 675). Not loaded: capital costs with no capacity (CHP USD 5-200+ M), effective electrical efficiency (no parameter), per-day rig diesel use (not per metre), chart-only figures (motor efficiency classes, BESS failure statistics, flywheel load profiles), qualitative selection tables. Derived values carry a formula (efficiency = power/fuel, capex per kW, capacity factor, % reductions). Heating-value basis: furnaces/boilers LHV stated; CHP case premises LHV; elsewhere not stated. Many numbers reprinted from cited works (noted).
